texts.li: Word has come down the roads: {X_nameDef}, the son of {DEAD}, has sworn to avenge his {RELATION}, and young fighters of {FACTION} have gathered to him. They have made camp somewhere near the colony, and nobody has seen where yet.\n\n{DEAD} died at the colony's hands. The son means to finish what {TALE} began.

[hisLowtech] {FACTION} tell it at their fires: {X_nameDef}, the son of {DEAD}, cut his hair short on the day he heard how his {RELATION} died, and has called up every young spear who would follow him. They are camped in the hills within a few days of the colony.\n\nWhere, nobody has said. Whoever is out beyond the walls should watch for smoke.

[hisHightech] A trader passing through brought the news: {X_nameDef}, the son of {DEAD}, has put a crew together among {FACTION}, armed it out of what was left of {TALE}, and set up somewhere within a few days of the colony.\n\nNobody knows where yet. He is in no hurry to say.

[their:foe,!slayer] Word has come down the roads: {X_nameDef}, the son of {DEAD}, has sworn to avenge his {RELATION}, and fighters of {FACTION} have gathered to him somewhere near the colony.\n\n{FACTION} have a name for the colony's people they hate most, and it is {FOE}. The son has heard it too.

[slayer] Word has come down the roads: {X_nameDef}, the son of {DEAD}, has sworn to avenge his {RELATION}, and fighters of {FACTION} have gathered to him. He has made camp somewhere near the colony.\n\nHe knows who brought {DEAD} down. {B_nameDef}'s name has been said at his fire more than once.

summaries.li: {X_nameDef}'s band is camped near the colony, hidden until someone out beyond the walls sees its smoke or a neighbour sends word. Once it is found, its raids come from its side of the map, led by {X_nameDef}, until the colony breaks the camp, pays its price, makes peace with {FACTION}, or beats its raids off.

texts.li: [killer] {X_nameDef} is dead, brought down by {B_nameDef}. The band he raised to avenge {DEAD} has lost the one who held it together.\n\nTwo of that family have now died fighting the colony. {FACTION} will tell it for a long time.
[!killer] {X_nameDef} is dead. The band he raised in {DEAD}'s name has lost the one who held it together, and {FACTION} have lost the last of that family's fighters.

li.chronicle: {X_nameDef}, the son of {DEAD}, died fighting the colony.

texts.li: {X_nameDef}, who came to avenge {DEAD}, is in the colony's hands. His band will not stay a band for long without him.\n\nWhat becomes of him is up to the colony now.

li.chronicle: The colony took {X_nameDef}, the son of {DEAD}, alive.

texts.li: {X_nameDef}'s band has broken up, and he has ridden on with the few who stayed with him. {DEAD} is not avenged, and the colony is not sorry.

li.chronicle: {X_nameDef}, the son of {DEAD}, gave up his revenge and rode on.

texts.li: [own] Word has come from {PLACE}: {X_nameDef}, the son of {DEAD}, is on the road to the colony with one companion and no weapon drawn. {FACTION} say he has something to ask the colony about his {RELATION}.

[among] {X_nameDef}, the son of {DEAD}, has been living among {FACTION} since {TALE} came to its end, and wants no part in his {RELATION}'s war. Word has come that he is on the road to the colony with one companion, to ask the colony something.

[afterEnd:ransomed,own] {DEAD} came home from the colony's cells bought back with silver, and the family has not said much since. Now word has come from {PLACE} that {X_nameDef}, the son, is on the road to the colony with one companion and no weapon drawn.

[afterEnd:handedOver] The colony handed {DEAD} over to be judged by others, and the family of {DEAD} has had a long while to think about it. Word has come that {X_nameDef}, the son, is on the road to the colony with one companion, riding with {FACTION} and meaning no harm.

summaries.li: He will come to the gate and ask something of the colony. What it answers is his family's to remember.

texts.li: [ask:father] {X_nameDef} stands at the colony's gate with his companion, hat in hand. His {RELATION}, {DEAD}, is in the colony's cells, and he has come to ask that {DEAD} be let go with him.\n\n"The band is gone," he says. "There is nobody left for {DEAD} to lead. Let me take my {RELATION} home."

[ask:meet] {X_nameDef} stands at the colony's gate with his companion. He has heard that {DEAD}, his {RELATION}, lives at the colony now, one of its own people, and he asks only to see {A_nameDef} with his own eyes and talk a while at the gate.

[ask:grave] {X_nameDef} stands at the colony's gate with his companion. His {RELATION}, {DEAD}, lies in one of the colony's graves, and he asks that someone of the colony lay a token of the family's on it and say the words for {DEAD} that he cannot say from outside the wall.

[ask:blade,hisLowtech] {X_nameDef} stands at the colony's gate with his companion. His {RELATION}'s {ITEM} lies in the colony's stores, he says, taken when {DEAD} fell, and it is the last thing of the family's anyone could hand down. He asks for it back.

[ask:blade,hisHightech] {X_nameDef} stands at the colony's gate with his companion. {DEAD}'s {ITEM} is in the colony's stores, he says, and it is the only thing of his {RELATION}'s he has any hope of getting back. He asks for it.

[ask:peace] {X_nameDef} stands at the colony's gate with his companion, no weapon drawn. There is nothing of {DEAD}'s left at the colony for him to ask for, he says; what he wants is a peace between his family and the colony, so that the next of them does not come here to settle {TALE}'s account.

li.label: Let {DEAD} go with his son
li.outcome: The council agrees. A warden walks {DEAD} out of the cells to the gate, and {RELATION} and son go home together. {X_nameDef} says the family will not forget it.

li.label: Let {A_nameDef} go out to him
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} walks out to the gate to see the son {A_pronoun} has not seen since {TALE}. What they say to each other is theirs.

li.label: Have {A_nameDef} lay his token on the grave
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} gives {A_nameDef} a small token of the family's at the gate, and {A_nameDef} carries it to {DEAD}'s grave and stays there a while, as he asked.
li.deed: laid a token of {X_nameDef}'s on {DEAD}'s grave

li.label: Give him back {ITEM}
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} carries {DEAD}'s {ITEM} out of the stores to the gate and puts it in {X_nameDef}'s hands.

li.label: Make peace with him
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} goes out to the gate and the two of them agree it: no one of {DEAD}'s family will come to the colony with a weapon on account of {TALE}, and the colony bears the family no ill will.
li.deed: made peace with {X_nameDef}, the son of {DEAD}

li.label: Send him away
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} is told the colony has nothing for him. He looks at the wall a long moment, then turns and goes back the way he came.

texts.li: {DEAD} has been let go from the colony's cells, and {X_nameDef} took his {RELATION} home. The family of {DEAD} owes the colony a good turn now, and {FACTION} know it.

li.chronicle: The colony let {DEAD} go home with {X_nameDef}.

texts.li: {X_nameDef} has gone home, after a long talk at the gate with the {RELATION} who chose the colony over {TALE}. Whatever passed between them, he left without a hard word for anyone.

li.chronicle: {X_nameDef} came to the gate to see {DEAD}.

texts.li: {X_nameDef} has gone home. His family's token lies on {DEAD}'s grave inside the colony's wall, and he will tell his people the colony did that much for his {RELATION}.

li.chronicle: The colony laid a token of {X_nameDef}'s on {DEAD}'s grave.

texts.li: {X_nameDef} has gone home with {DEAD}'s {ITEM}. It will hang where his family can see it, and the family will remember who gave it back.

titles.li: A peace with the family of {DEAD}

texts.li: {X_nameDef} has gone home with the colony's word, and left his own. The family of {DEAD} will not come to the colony to settle {TALE}'s account, and the colony has one quarrel fewer in the world.

li.chronicle: The colony made peace with {X_nameDef}, the son of {DEAD}.

texts.li: {X_nameDef} has gone home with nothing. Whatever he tells his family about the colony, it will not be kind.

li.chronicle: The colony sent {X_nameDef}, the son of {DEAD}, away from its gate.

texts.li: [hunted,among] {ENEMY} brought {DEAD} down, and they have not stopped there: {X_nameDef}, the son, has been on the run ever since, turned out by his own people and sheltering with {FACTION}. Word has come that he is making for the colony.

[hunted,own] {ENEMY} brought {DEAD} down, and they have not stopped there: {X_nameDef}, the son, has been on the run ever since, and his own people are afraid to keep him. Word has come that he is making for the colony.

[!hunted] {DEAD} was brought down out in the world, and {X_nameDef}, the son, has been on the run ever since with one companion, sheltering where he can. Word has come that he is making for the colony.

[hunted,hisLowtech] The hunters who ran {DEAD} down are hunting the son now. {X_nameDef} has been sleeping in barns and ditches since, with one companion who would not leave him, and word has come that he is making for the colony.

summaries.li: He will come to the gate asking shelter. Taking in the son of a warlord may cost the colony the goodwill of those who hunt him.

texts.li: {X_nameDef}, the son of {DEAD}, is at the colony's gate with one companion and almost nothing else. He asks shelter: a place inside the wall, work to earn it, and a while out of sight of the road.\n\n"I was a boy holding the horses when {TALE} rode out," he says.

[hunted] {X_nameDef}, the son of {DEAD}, is at the colony's gate with one companion, both of them thin and footsore. {ENEMY} are hunting him for what his {RELATION} did, he says, and he asks the colony to take him in.\n\n"I can work," he says. "I would rather work for you than hang for {DEAD}."

li.label: Take them in
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} and his companion come in through the gate. They have a roof now, and the colony has two more hands.

outcomes.li: [huntersAtWar] {X_nameDef} and his companion come in through the gate. {ENEMY} will hear of it, and they are already at war with the colony.

li.label: A few nights' rest, then the road
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} and his companion may sleep by the wall for two nights and go on rested. He thanks the colony, and does not ask again.

li.label: Turn him away
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} is told there is no room at the colony for the son of {DEAD}. He nods as if he expected it, and the two of them go back to the road.

texts.li: {X_nameDef}, the son of {DEAD}, lives at the colony now. Whatever {TALE} was to the world, he is one of the colony's own here.

li.chronicle: The colony took in {X_nameDef}, the son of {DEAD}.

texts.li: {X_nameDef} has gone on down the road, rested and fed. Where he goes from here, the colony will probably never know.

li.chronicle: The colony gave {X_nameDef}, the son of {DEAD}, two nights' rest.

texts.li: {X_nameDef} has gone back to the road. The colony has no part in what becomes of him.

li.chronicle: The colony turned {X_nameDef}, the son of {DEAD}, away.

texts.li: {TALE} is gone, and so is {DEAD}, nobody is sure where. What is left of the band is {X_nameDef}, the son, and the few who would not go home: word has come that they are riding the region looking for work, and the colony is on their road.

[hisLowtech] When {TALE} broke up, a handful of its young fighters stayed together under {X_nameDef}, the son of {DEAD}. They have spears and horses and no war to use them on, and they are coming the colony's way.

[hisHightech] {X_nameDef}, the son of {DEAD}, has kept a few of {TALE}'s fighters together since the band broke up. They have rifles, a little ammunition and no employer, and word has come that they are heading for the colony.

summaries.li: They will come to the gate looking for work. The colony can take them on, feed them and send them on, or send them on hungry.

texts.li: {X_nameDef}, the son of {DEAD}, is at the colony's gate with what is left of {TALE}: a few young fighters, armed and hungry. They are looking for work, he says, any work that pays in food and a roof, and they can fight if the colony has need of that.\n\n"{TALE} is finished," he says. "We are not."

li.label: Take them on
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} and his riders come in through the gate, to work for their keep and fight when the colony fights.

li.label: A meal, and the road
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} brings them a hot meal at the gate. They eat it standing, thank the colony, and ride on.

li.label: Send them on
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} is told the colony has no work for him. The riders turn their horses and go.

outcomes.li: [hisHightech] {X_nameDef} is told the colony has no work for him. The riders shoulder their rifles and go.

texts.li: {X_nameDef} and his riders live at the colony now. The last of {TALE} works the colony's fields and stands on its wall.

li.chronicle: The colony took on {X_nameDef}, the son of {DEAD}, and his riders.

texts.li: {X_nameDef} and his riders have gone on, fed. If they find work somewhere, they will remember where they ate on the way.

li.chronicle: The colony fed the riders of {X_nameDef}, the son of {DEAD}.

texts.li: {X_nameDef} and his riders have gone on, looking for work somewhere else.

li.chronicle: The colony sent the riders of {X_nameDef}, the son of {DEAD}, on their way.
